issues.title: Agro 2/2026 Appendix 3 is the January sheet
issues.detail: Appendix 3 'Crop Statistic (2026)' in Agro 2/2026 repeats January 2026 from Agro 1/2026 (1,708.16 t, 0.85 t/ha, this month = to date, with #DIV/0! cells). It gives no Jan–Aug tonnage, so FFB tonnes stay at PA Jan–Jun 8,765.54 t while yield Jan–Aug is 6.61 t/ha (Table 15). Ask for the August sheet.

issues.title: Rat damage: threshold and status conflict
issues.detail: PA 2/2026 para 6.6.1.1 uses a 10% threshold and calls damage quite extensive. Agro 2/2026 para 4.5.3 uses a 20% acceptance level and says generally under control. On 20%, A and B are at the level, not above it, though para 4.5.2 calls them above threshold. Para 4.5.2 dates the census June, but A and B were 28 Mar–20 Apr. Table 12 is unchanged from the PA, so there is no census after June despite 'as August 2026'. Baiting Round 3 % column simply equals the census % (A 20%, C5 10%); rounds 1–3 in the same month for A; F baited July though the PA reports to June with all done.

issues.title: Corrective pruning: done (PA) vs ongoing (Agro)
issues.detail: PA 2/2026 (visit 29 Jul) says corrective pruning was completed, balance nil in every block. Agro 2/2026 paras 4.1.3 and 4.3.4 say P05A3 and P05A5 were under corrective pruning in Aug–Sep because pruning was overdue, significantly behind schedule. PA also calls the 13-day interval satisfactory while Agro records over 30 days in A3 and A5 in Aug, and its Table 6 still shows A at 13-14 days (based on harvested area, para 4.1.3).

issues.title: Flooding as cause of 2026 manuring delay
issues.detail: Agro 2/2026 paras 3.1 and 5.8 blame flooding and labour; para 4.2.7 says no heavy rainfall events causing major flooding were recorded up to Aug 2026. PA 2/2026 para 6.4.2 blames late Mix B delivery and caked NK1.

issues.title: Fertiliser Table 4: applied exceeds received
issues.detail: Agro 2/2026 Table 4: Mix B applied 831.05 t but received to date 802.55 t; opening stock is not shown. Table 5 lists pending 'Block B,C,D,E,F,G'; there is no Block G (blocks are A–F and H).

issues.title: Spraying Table 11 and para 4.4.1
issues.detail: Agro 2/2026 Table 11 gives Block D circle programme 569 ha; two rounds on 210.2 ha would be 420.4 ha, as used for inter-row (PA D circle was 509.20 to June). On 420.4 ha D would not be 63%. Para 4.4.1 says Blocks B, C, D behind on circle and then 'Blocks A and C had not yet completed', 'B and F ahead', which does not fit the table for circle (A 103%, B 83%).

issues.title: Agro 2/2026 leaf table errors
issues.detail: Table 7 prints C1 Mg 0.59%; the lab sheet in Appendix 2 shows 0.29%. Status labels are inconsistent: N 2.63 is ML at E2 but N at F5; Cu 3.73 is L at A5 but N at E1; Ca 0.55–0.56 is N at D and C but ML at F5–F6. Para 4.2.2 says majors are normal to high, but several N, P and all A/B Ca are ML. ZnCu is given as 15% Zn, 10% Cu in para 4.2.2 but 15% Cu, 10% Zn in Appendix 1.

issues.title: Roads and mounding: table remarks
issues.detail: Agro 2/2026 Table 8 marks 12x10x8 ft desilting (317.05 of 850 chains) and the canal (702 of 2,000 m) 'Completed'. Remounding budget is 27,848 palms in Agro, 27,484 in PA. Lateriting moved from 0 (PA June) to 649.35 chains. Agro 1/2026 cited 32,054 of 34,305 palms mounded earlier.

issues.title: Agro 2/2026 small inconsistencies
issues.detail: Table 6 omits Jan and Apr 2026. Para 4.1.2 says PM05D stayed within 12–15 days, but Table 6 has 13-16 in Feb. Appendix 1(b) gives RP 2.00 kg for H, others 1.50. Senior Manager: Agro prints En Mohd Shafirun Bin Mohd Azba; PA prints Mr Chan Wah Vee. Pruning programme 15,998.64 ha is 8 rounds to August, not a full-year figure as labelled 'Programme 2026'.

issues.title: Fertiliser doses below agronomist's programme
issues.detail: PA 2/2026 manuring tables show later-round doses lower than Agro 1/2026 Appendix 1. Examples: PM05A and PM06E rounds 4-5, and PM06F1-3/F6 rounds 4-5, are 1500 g + 1250 g per palm (Agro: 2000 g + 1750 g); PM05B rounds 3-4 are 1500 g + 1250 g (Agro: 2000 g + 1750 g); PM19H rounds 4-5 are 1500 g each (Agro: 2000 g each). PM05C and PM05D have only 3 rounds in the PA; Agro lists a 4th round of NK1/NK2 2000 g. PM06F4-F5 have no 5th round in PA (Agro: 2000 g). The Agro GMD comment says the 2026 programme should be adjusted for the deferred final 2025 Mix B round, but Agro Appendix 1 still shows the full doses and neither report explains the lower PA doses. Needs confirmation from the agronomist. Agro 2/2026 para 3.4 now records Mix B at 1.5 kg/palm in P06E-5, matching the PA dose, with no comment on the change; it says scheduled August (PA programme: July).

issues.title: Manuring hectares: budget does not match block tables
issues.detail: PA 2/2026 para 6.4.1 gives 2,872.90 ha manured out of 5,039.74 ha budgeted (57%). The ACT columns of the PA block tables do add up to 2,872.90 ha, so the achieved figure is consistent. The to-June programme in the same block tables adds up to about 4,906 ha, not 5,039.74 ha (about 59% done on that base). The PM19H table also shows 'TOTAL 354.54' ha for a 2.43 ha block.

issues.title: PA uses 136 SPH; Agro census found far fewer palms
issues.detail: PA 2/2026 rat census assumes 136 SPH everywhere (e.g. PM05A 51,680 palms, PM05B 45,560 palms, 271,646 in total). Agro 1/2026 Table 3: the 2025 census found PM05A 49,598 (131 SPH), PM05B 38,100 (114 SPH), PM06E 43,469 (126 SPH) and PM06F 38,681 (123 SPH). PM05B is 7,460 palms below the PA figure (16%). Agro prints the differences as -4%, -20%, -8% and -10%, which divide by the new count; on the 136 SPH base they are -4%, -16%, -7% and -9%. Agro 2/2026 Table 3 keeps the census SPH, yet its rat Table 12 uses 136 SPH for every block (e.g. Block A 51,680 palms vs 49,598).

issues.title: PA 'June 2026' bunch weights equal Agro's January 2026 figures
issues.detail: PA 2/2026 para 8.5 gives June 2026 bunch weights A 12.8, B 11.6, C 20.1, D 19.2, E 13.2, F 13.1 and P19H 8.0 kg. Agro 1/2026 Appendix 3(b) gives January 2026 ABW of 12.82, 11.58, 20.15, 19.20, 13.20, 13.10 and 8.00 kg. These match to rounding, so the PA's June column may be January data. The 'abnormal' P19H increase the PA flags may come from this.

issues.title: PA last-year 12-month crop is budget, not 2025 actual
issues.detail: PA 2/2026 crop table's last-year '12 months budget' column shows 33,785 t (16.89 t/ha). Agro 1/2026 reports the 2025 actual as 25,434.05 t (12.72 t/ha; Appendix 3(a) and para 5.2). Directors should not compare the PA's 16.89 t/ha with actual yields.

issues.title: Rat damage: under control (Agro) vs extensive (PA)
issues.detail: Agro 1/2026 (Dec 2025 census) shows 1-4% damage in every field, says baiting is not required and calls the rat population under control. PA 2/2026 census for Mar-Jun 2026 shows 10-20% damage (18% overall, above the 10% threshold), and 3 baiting rounds were done. This could be a real surge in under 6 months. The PA census also shows exactly 20% in all 11 sub-blocks of PM05A and PM05B, which looks estimated rather than counted.

issues.title: Area statement differs between reports
issues.detail: PA 2/2026 gives total estate area 2,016.00 ha, including 9.71 ha unplanted. Agro 1/2026 and 2/2026 Table 1 give 2,023.00 ha, including 16.71 ha unplantable. Planted area agrees at 1,999.83 ha. The PA also labels its 16.17 ha non-planted subtotal 'Total Estate Hectarage'.

issues.title: Pruning table errors in PA
issues.detail: PA 2/2026 pruning table shows PM05B 1,621.92 ha done of 2,010.00 ha as '23%'; the correct figure is 81%. Para 6.5.3 says 626 ha of corrective pruning was carried forward from 2025, but the same table lists a corrective backlog of 1,298.63 ha (all marked done).

issues.title: Agro yield-change percentages use the wrong base
issues.detail: Agro 1/2026 Tables 15 and 17 divide the change by the newer year, not the older one. PM05A January is shown as -226% (0.75 to 0.23 t/ha); the correct change is -69%. PM05A 2025 is shown as -41%; it is -29% on the 2024 base. Table 17 also gives PM05B January 2025 as 0.30 t/ha, but Appendix 3(b) gives 44.49 t, or 0.13 t/ha (Appendix 3(b) is used on the dashboard). PM06E is 0.79 in Table 17 vs 0.76 in Appendix 3(b).

issues.title: Agro 2025 fertiliser stock does not balance
issues.detail: Agro 1/2026 Table 4: Mix B applied 1,647.95 t, but 2024 carry-forward plus receipts total only 1,534.6 t (29.3 + 1,505.3). Completion is 1,647.95 / 2,191.7 = 75%; the report says 74%.

issues.title: Agro ABW figure inconsistent
issues.detail: Agro 1/2026 para 5.6 gives 2025 average bunch weight as 19.30 kg. Its own Appendix 3(a) shows 25,434.05 t from 1,731,241 bunches, which is about 14.7 kg. Block ABWs in Appendix 3(a) and PA para 8.5 (11.6-20.1 kg) also do not support 19.30 kg.

issues.title: Other typos
issues.detail: Agro 1/2026 Appendix 1(b) shows P19/H1 as 68.52 ha (it is 2.43 ha). Agro 2023 rainfall shows 180 rain days, but the monthly figures add up to 204 (the November to-date figure does not carry forward). PA 2/2026 summary page is headed 'PA REPORT: PSK ESTATE 1/2026'. kb:
LADANG PSK (Rangkai Sempurna Sdn Bhd, Prosper group). Fact pack built from PARAS reports: Planting Advisory (PA) Report 2/2026 by Mr Boey Chee Weng, visit 29 July 2026, reviewing January to June 2026; Agronomy Report 2/2026 by Mr Alison Janari (Junior Agronomist) and Chong Kuan Ming (Senior Agronomist), visit 22 September 2026, with data to August 2026; and, for older facts, Agronomy Report 1/2026, visit 12 February 2026 (called Agro below where no number is given). General Manager Mr Lee Chong Yew. Senior Manager per PA: Mr Chan Wah Vee (Agro report listed En Mohd Shafirun Bin Mohd Azba). Estate Manager: En Khairol Amir Bin Idris (joined company 2 May 2025, estate 1 Sep 2025).

AGRONOMY 2/2026 (visit 22 Sep 2026, data as of Aug 2026). YIELD Jan-Aug 2026 (Table 15, Period 8): 6.61 t/ha vs 7.88 in Jan-Aug 2025 (-16%). By field 2026 vs 2025: A 3.43 vs 6.28 (-45%), B 5.78 vs 6.23 (-7%), C 8.2 vs 10.68 (-23%), D 8.5 vs 9.77 (-13%), E 7.43 vs 7.27 (+2%), F 6.95 vs 7.24 (-4%), H 22.04 vs 10.44 (+111%, only 2.43 ha). No Jan-Aug tonnage is printed; Appendix 3 repeats January 2026. Main limiting factors: extended harvesting intervals, pruning delays, late fertiliser.
ROUNDS to Aug (Table 16): average 14.37, 90% of target; A 9.8 (61%), B 13.3 (83%), C 15.33 (96%), D 16.03 (100%), E 14.85 (93%), F 14.5 (91%), H 16.8 (105%). Intervals improved from 18-20 days at worst in Feb-Mar to 12-15 days in most fields by Jul-Aug, but P05A3 and P05A5 went over 30 days in August with no harvesting recorded, overripe and rotten bunches, from few harvesters and corrective pruning. Additional harvesters recruited, number not printed. B1 crop quality acceptable, some long stalks. EV crawler in use, no overnight bunches.
MANURING as of Aug (Table 4), required/received/applied t: Mix B 1,228.7/802.55/831.05 = 68%; RP 134.65/134.65/126.5 = 94%; NK 338.35/281.4/247.05 = 73%. Causes given: flooding and labour in first half. About one round behind for Jul-Aug; Mix B Jul/Aug/Sep pending 1-2 months in Blocks B to F. Estate targets November 2026. Block A second-half fertiliser was stopped for possible 2028 replanting; Agro says continue until confirmed, stopping only one year before replanting; GMD must be consulted. Quality at E5 acceptable (Mix B 1,500 g/palm, 30 bags per worker). EFB at P05B1, 40 mt/ha, poorly applied, no records.
SPRAYING as of Aug (Table 11): circle 3,697.04 of 4,148.08 ha = 89% (A 103, B 83, C 78, D 63, E 100, F 104, H 100); inter-row 4,075.49 of 3,999.66 ha = 102% (A 98, B 107, C 86, D 100, E 100, F 125, H 100). Clidemia hirta in D1, C1, C2, D3, F1; bracken on peat; VOPs persist and need a dedicated round.
PRUNING as of Aug (Table 10): 12,470.5 of 15,998.64 ha = 78%: A 79, B 86, C 88, D 67, E 88, F 51, H 100. New workers recruited Sep 2026; intensive pruning, back on schedule expected by end 2026. A3, A5 well behind.
LEAF (samples received 28 May 2026, results 4 Jul 2026): majors normal to high, B adequate, Zn borderline, Cu mostly low on peat; ZnCu 150 g/palm advised. PEAT: water table within range, palms greener, but bunches smaller than standard. New 5x4x3 ft drain in Block A 188.60 of 1,000 chains; lateriting 649.35 of 1,240 chains; remounding 0 of 27,848 palms (PA 27,484); backhoe 1,390 of 1,900 hours. Rain Jan-Aug 2026 1,569.50 mm, 66 days; Sept to date 185 mm, 4 days.
PESTS: rat table repeats PA census (18%); Agro says generally under control; 20% acceptance level (PA uses 10%). Barn owl 50 of 109 boxes occupied = 46%, poor; D 0 of 17, E 3 of 18; 31 new boxes installed by Aug. Ganoderma localised, census in progress; suspected dead palms in C1, C2.
2027 PROGRAMME (Appendix 1, g/palm): A, B, E: Feb Mix C 2,000, Mar CuZn 150, May Mix B 1,750, Jul Mix C 2,000, Sep Mix B 1,750. C, D, F4, F5: Jan Mix B 2,000, Apr Mix B 2,000, Jun RP 1,500, Jul Mix B 2,000, Oct Mix B 2,000. F1-F3, F6: Feb Mix C 2,000, Mar CuZn 150, May Mix B 1,750, Aug Mix C 2,000, Oct Mix B 1,750. H: Jan, Apr, Jul, Oct Mix B 2,000, Jun RP 2,000.
GMD COMMENTS (30 Oct 2026): yield unsatisfactory, mainly incomplete crop recovery and deviations from manuring; strict adherence, no deviation; explain P05A crop recovery and the EFB programme; update census; rectify P05A pruning; address barn owls.

AREA (PA 2/2026). All 1,999.83 ha planted is mature oil palm. PM05 A1-A6 380.00 ha, PM05 B1-B5 335.00, PM05 C1-C6 414.55, PM05 D1-D3 210.20 (all planted 2005), PM06 E1-E6 344.00, PM06 F1-F6 313.65 (2006), PM19H 2.43 (2019). No immature or replant. Except for part of P19H, palms are over 20 years old and in the declining-yield stage (Agro). Much of the estate is peat and low-lying and floods often. Agro: flooding used to last up to six months; after canal desilting, water now recedes in about 60 days.

PALM CENSUS (Agro 1/2026 Table 3). PM05A 49,598 palms, 131 SPH (-4%); PM05B 38,100, 114 SPH (printed -20%, calculates to -16%); PM06E 43,469, 126 SPH (printed -8%, about -7%); PM06F 38,681, 123 SPH (printed -10%, about -9%). All completed 2025. PM05C (56,379), PM05D (28,587) and PM19H (330) are still in progress at the assumed 136 SPH. The GMD said the census was far too slow; PARAS will help with drone/GIS census and topographic mapping.

LABOUR (PA, June 2026). Harvesters 52 vs 83 required (short 31; 1:38 ha vs 1:24 ha required). By July harvesters were 66 (1:30 ha), still 17 short; 17 more were expected in August-September. Drivers/loaders 8 of 9, weeding 10 of 18, manuring 6 of 8, mandore 0 of 1, pruning 2 of 21. Total 78 vs 140 (short 62). Workers to planted ha 1:26 vs ideal 1:12. Agro (Feb) reported a shortage of 48 workers, mainly harvesters, high turnover, and 6 new TKI workers arriving 30 Jan 2026. The PA and GMD call harvester shortage and turnover the main problem, and say it has dragged on too long.

STAFF (PA). Big reshuffle: En Mohd Bukhari (Asst) in from Insan Jaya from July; Mr Supitor (Asst) out to Juasa A from July; En Mohd Afiq out to Tagar 3 from April; En Aiman (Cadet) in from Tagar 3 from April; En Mohd Taufiq promoted from Field Conductor from Nov 2025. CIRCLE SPRAYING (PA). 3,061.60 ha (1.5 rounds) of 3,278.95 ha (1.6 rounds) = 93%. By field: A 117%, B 90%, C 91%, D 35%, E 96%, F 130%, H 50%. Circles generally clean. CKS high-volume sprayers used at 4.4 ha/manday; PA reckons 6 ha/manday is possible, and Inter Pumps have been ordered. Piece rate RM15/ha, earnings RM66/day vs basic RM65.38. Glyphosate 0.3 l/ha. Only 9 pumps/manday (potential 12); sprayers work only 4.5 hours a day. GMD: use pure glyphosate, no Ally.

SELECTIVE SPRAYING (PA). 3,384.03 ha (1.7 rounds) of 3,999.41 ha (2 rounds) = 85%. A 72%, B 103%, C 60%, D 94%, E 100%, F 89%, H 100%. Inter-rows have improved drastically, woodies are cleared, and the new EM was praised. VOPs, Stenochlaena, brackens and Giant Paspalum remain. Mist blowers at 4.5 ha/manday, RM16/ha, earnings RM72/day, Garlon 0.36 l/ha, 6 pumps/day vs potential 10. 2025 full year: circle 56%, inter-row 63%. Post-flood broadleaf regrowth needs selective spraying.

MANURING. PA: 2,872.90 ha of 5,039.74 ha budgeted manured to June (57%); the ACT columns of the PA block tables add up to 2,872.90 ha, but the to-June programme in those tables adds up to about 4,906 ha, not 5,039.74 ha. The delay came from late Mix B delivery and caked NK1. Wheelbarrow application at 30 bags/manday, RM2.30/bag, RM69/day. Manuring cost RM1,107,900 vs budget RM1,475,886. EFB: only 54.11 ha of 624.70 ha, because the GM diverted EFB to the Juasa A and B immature areas. EFB rate 40 t/ha, transport RM11/t, levelling RM1.50/t. PRUNING. PA: corrective pruning completed (626 ha carried forward from 2025; table backlog 1,298.63 ha). Progressive pruning 8,041.42 of 11,998.98 ha = 67%: A 66%, B 81% (table misprints 23%), C 66%, D 60%, E 85%, F 39%, H 83%. A task force is pruning unpruned palms in flood areas at no extra cost. Rates per ha per year: 2005 RM120, 2006 RM100, 2019 RM70; corrective RM100/ha. Agro: 2025 pruning only 74% (5,928.37 of 7,999.32 ha). By January 2026 it was 32%, with nothing done in P05A, P05D or P19H; under-pruning in D3, B4 and C6 was hurting harvesting.

PESTS AND DISEASE. Agro (Dec 2025 census): rat damage 1-4%, under control, no baiting needed. Barn owl boxes 109; 50 good, 59 poor; 46% occupied (PM05D 0 of 17, PM06E 17%). PA (census Mar-Jun 2026): damage 18% overall; A and B 20%, C 14%, D 17%, E 17%, F 17%. 3 baiting rounds done; rats to be censused quarterly and baited above 10%. Ganoderma: sporadic infections, fruiting bodies and upper stem rot in P05C2 (PA).

ROADS AND DRAINS (PA). Grading and compaction 2,643 of 2,650 chains at RM19/chain (on budget); road condition very good. Lateriting 1,240 chains budgeted, none done. Desilting: 8x6x4 ft 2,178 of 2,100 chains (RM46); 12x10x8 ft 317 of 850 chains (RM51); 30x12x10 ft canal 702 of 2,000 (table says metres) at RM520. Mounding: 27,484 palms budgeted at RM8.50/palm, none done (PA). Agro says 32,054 of 34,305 palms (93%) were mounded earlier.

HARVESTING (PA). Cost RM629,068 = RM71.77/t vs budget RM81.53/t (harvest labour 47.51, transport 19.62, incentive 1.23, top-up 3.41). 10.2 rounds vs 12 budgeted; average interval 13 days per PA (should be at most 13-14 days); outturn 95%. 12 crawlers (2 cutters + 1 collector) and 3 Badang (3 + 1); 2 EV tricycles bought for trial. Harvest rates RM45-49/t budget, RM39-40/t labour, average earnings RM67-78/day vs basic RM65.39. Agro: January 2026 intervals up to 49 days in A and 50 in B; 2025 rounds averaged 18.45 (77% of target), with A at 14.17 (59%). Overripe bunches 4-5% in P05C-06 and 8-10% in P05E-6.

CROP (PA, Jan-Jun 2026). FFB 8,765.54 t vs estimate 15,573 t (annual budget 33,146 t). Same period 2025: 10,903.58 t. Yield 4.38 t/ha vs budget 7.79 t/ha (-44%) and 5.45 t/ha last year (-20%). CPO 1,386.39 t, OER 15.82% (budget 18.51%); KER 5.00%. PA's last-year '12 months budget' column shows 33,785 t / 16.89 t/ha; this is a budget, and the Agro 2025 actual was 25,434.05 t / 12.72 t/ha. Bunch weights per PA (June 2025 to June 2026): A 13.9 to 12.8, B 13.5 to 11.6, C 18.0 to 20.1, D 18.2 to 19.2, E 13.6 to 13.2, F 14.5 to 13.1, P19H 2.6 to 8.0 kg. Causes of the shortfall: harvester shortage, low-crop season and flooded peat. Agro yields (full years): 2024 12.89 and 2025 12.72 t/ha; by field 2025 A 7.85, B 11.80, C 18.22, D 14.59, E 11.52, F 12.33, H 19.59. January 2026 only: 0.85 t/ha vs 0.83 in January 2025 (+2%).

COST OF PRODUCTION (PA, to June). RM389.93 per t FFB vs estimate RM320.56 (annual budget RM301.22): general charges 108.51 vs 93.34; upkeep 209.65 vs 145.70; harvesting 71.77 vs 81.53. Per t CPO RM2,465.33 vs RM1,731.58. Cost is high because crop is below budget. Capex RM16,358 vs budget RM17,110 (computers, staff quarters furniture, fibre boat).

RAINFALL (Agro Appendix 2). 2023: 4,215.5 mm (stated 180 rain days; monthly rows add to 204). 2024: 3,770.5 mm, 136 days. 2025: 3,637.5 mm, 131 days. January 2026: 101 mm in 6 days.

ADVISORS' BOTTOM LINE. PA: recruit harvesters and sprayers, switch to Inter Pumps, raise pumps per manday and hours worked, clear the pruning backlog, start mounding, train the new Assistants, and fix prolonged flooding. Agro: keep strictly to the fertiliser programme, since deviations over two years have depressed yield and bunch weight; shorten harvest intervals; speed up census; maintain barn owl boxes.
